missing_details: The field F must be assumed perfect
The cohomological dimension of F must be specified as at most 2
G must be a semisimple simply connected algebraic group defined over F
H¹(F,G) denotes the (pointed) first Galois cohomology set of F with coefficients in G
Triviality of H¹(F,G) means it consists only of the distinguished identity class
refined_question: Let F be a perfect field whose (Galois) cohomological dimension is at most 2. Let G be a semisimple algebraic group over F which is simply connected. Is the pointed set H¹(F,G) of Galois cohomology classes (equivalently, F-isomorphism classes of G-torsors) trivial, consisting only of the identity class?
justification: The title “Serre’s conjecture II” alone does not specify the nature of the field F (perfectness), the bound on its cohomological dimension, the fact that G must be simply connected and semisimple over F, nor that H¹(F,G) refers to the pointed Galois cohomology set whose triviality is asserted. Hence a low completeness score of 3. The refined question explicitly states all hypotheses: F is perfect with cd(F)≤2, G is a simply connected semisimple F-group, and H¹(F,G) is the pointed Galois cohomology set whose triviality is the conjecture.
